request.what: Annual funding for MLabs Core Tool Maintenance & Enhancement for Plutarch and Ply, including maintenance, compatibility, bug fixes, optimizations, documentation, and developer-experience improvements.

claims.claim: Plutarch is a Haskell eDSL for creating efficient Cardano smart contracts through controlled compilation into UPLC, and Ply serializes Plutarch scripts to and from CIP-57 blueprint-style artifacts with inferred types.
MLabs counted at least 26 teams building with Plutarch and Ply in a recent internal audit, while the rationale later states a conservative count of at least 15 teams.
Plutarch scripts rank among the smallest in MLabs' public cross-language benchmark suite while requiring comparatively low on-chain compute and memory.

The requested funding is intended to keep Plutarch and Ply reliable, compatible, and useful for Cardano builders as ledger, Plutus, and tooling evolve, including possible Dijkstra-era compatibility if relevant changes land during the funding period.
The proposal says it aligns with Cardano 2030 Pillar 2 by supporting developer experience, open-source SDKs, frameworks, and infrastructure.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and was advanced for on-chain Treasury Withdrawal submission.
The proposer states the requested amount does not, alone or in aggregate at submission, breach the applicable 350M ada Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.
The budget allocates 1,128,880 ada to Plutarch and Ply maintenance, compatibility, and developer experience, plus a 33,866 ada Intersect Budget Administration fee.
MLabs discloses prior treasury or ecosystem funding for Plutarch, Ply, related tooling, and Conway-era Plutarch work, including Project Catalyst and Intersect funding amounts.

Intersect will administer funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, role-based approvals, oversight entities, milestone-based disbursement controls, and a public dashboard.

summary: The proposal requests 1,162,746 ada for annual Plutarch and Ply maintenance and enhancement, provides a high-level work package and governance process references, and relies partly on checkable external links but also on internal adoption assertions and limited granular delivery detail.
